paper.title: The simulation of the movement of fish schools

headline: Huth-Wissel 1992 fish schooling (zonal SPP fish): 1/3 locked clauses REPRO; averaging p=0.91 vs decision p=0.18 (gap +0.73); CV(NND) avg=0.60 vs dec=0.48

verdicts.gate: P1 averaging advantage: mean polarization p_avg - p_dec >= 0.15

reasons: CV(NND) under averaging = 0.603 is NOT smaller than under decision = 0.483 (mean NND avg=1.073, dec=2.151); the decision school is looser/more diffuse, which lowers its NND coefficient of variation

verdicts.gate: P3 both rules school: p_avg > 0.5 AND p_dec > 0.5
reasons: decision-rule polarization p_dec=0.176 (max over seeds 0.296) does NOT exceed 0.5: following the single nearest neighbour fails to build a polarized school, so the contrast is averaging-vs-near-disorder here, not a same-baseline advantage (averaging p_avg=0.906 does school)

extra.knob: ONLY the integration rule is switched: AVERAGING (all relevant neighbours) vs DECISION (the single nearest orientation/attraction neighbour); all zonal forces identical between arms
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the Huth-Wissel averaging-vs-decision integration contrast (the averaging advantage on school polarization) and would catch an artifact — a falsified cohesion/both-school clause is reported MISS

citations: Huth, A. & Wissel, C. (1992). The simulation of the movement of fish schools. Journal of Theoretical Biology 156(3):365-385. doi:10.1016/S0022-5193(05)80681-2.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the Huth-Wissel averaging-vs-decision integration contrast (polarization gap, CV of NND, both-school check)
